items.q: The odour table gives cabbage-like and rancid-butter odour as two separate rows sharing a single condition, tyrosinemia type I.
opts: True — one condition is written across both rows
False — cabbage-like marks tyrosinemia and rancid butter marks hawkinsinuria
False — rancid butter is paired with methyl malonic acidemia
True — and the same condition also explains the fish odour
items.exp: The table brackets 'Cabbage-like' and 'Rancid butter' against one entry: Tyrosinemia type I. Swimming pool is hawkinsinuria and fish urine is trimethylaminuria. (Book p741)

items.q: Match each odour in the second half of the table with its condition — 1) Acid smell 2) Sulfurous 3) Sweet … A) Beta ketothiolase deficiency B) Methyl malonic acidemia (MMA) C) Cystinuria D) Multiple carboxylase deficiency
items.exp: As printed: acid smell → methyl malonic acidemia (MMA), sulfurous → cystinuria, sweet → beta ketothiolase deficiency; the cat-urine odour belongs to multiple carboxylase deficiency. (Book p741)

items.q: A mother brings an infant whose urine smells of boiled fish; the child is otherwise well and the dipstick is unremarkable. The table directs you to:
items.exp: 'Fish urine' is the row for trimethylaminuria; cystinuria is the sulfurous row, PKU the musty/mousy row and MSUD the curry/maple-syrup row. (Book p741)
